snippet.title: Michael Jackson in Brazil – The Untold Story (Spike Lee’s Vision)
snippet.description:
Spike Lee delivers a keynote in Brazil including about the making of Michael Jackson's they don't care about us. Filmed in Rio de Janeiro and Salvador Bahia, Brazil.

Spike Lee is a legend in cinema and his talk in Rio de Janeiro was electric. Watch as he discusses the importance of cinema, the creative process in filmmaking, Brazilian film and the Afro Brazilian cinema movement. Politics and the importance of creativity in storytelling are also discussed in this powerful talk. Part 1

One54, hosted by Akbar and Godfrey, is a first of its kind podcast spotlighting the untold stories of African entertainers, athletes and business leaders. Through unfiltered conversations, this podcast reveals the challenges and culture clashes of growing up African in America.

Akbar Gbajabiamila is a former NFL player, sports analyst, and television host best known for co-hosting American Ninja Warrior and CBS' The Talk. Proud of his Nigerian heritage, he brings a dynamic presence to media, blending his athletic background with insightful commentary and a deep connection to his roots.

Godfrey Daneschmah is a comedian and actor who's resume spans over 30 years and known for his sharp wit, spot-on impressions, and energetic stand-up performances. Drawing from his Nigerian heritage, he infuses cultural insight into his comedy, making him a standout voice in the entertainment industry.

One54 - Celebrating Africa’s 54 Countries, One Story At A Time

snippet.title: Spike Lee’s Michael Jackson Block Party Returns for His 68th Birthday
snippet.description:
Spike Lee is bringing back his annual Michael Jackson Block Party in Brooklyn — on the day the King of Pop would have turned 68.

Event: BK Loves MJ
Date: Saturday, August 29, 2026
Place: Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn
Time: 12:00 PM – 7:00 PM
Entry: Free
DJ: DJ Spinna
Sponsor: Jordan Brand

The tradition started on August 29, 2009, weeks after Michael Jackson’s passing. The first celebration was planned for Fort Greene Park, then moved to Prospect Park because the crowd was too large. Brooklyn even declared it Michael Jackson Day.

Over the years the party has moved between Prospect Park, Bed-Stuy, and Fort Greene. After a four-year break, it returned in 2023 with tens of thousands of fans.

This year’s event comes after the success of the Michael biopic starring Jaafar Jackson, which introduced a new generation to his music.

Would you be in Fort Greene on the 29th?

snippet.title: Spike Lee on Michael Jackson and Bad 25 (69th Venice International Film Festival)
snippet.description:
Full film review at: http://myetvmedia.com/film-review/bad25-spike-lees-love-letter-to-michael-jackson/

Spike Lee's highly anticipated Bad25 celebrating Michael Jackson premiers at the 69th Venice Film Festival. Exceeding expectations, this outstanding documentary in honour of one of the greatest entertainers of our time, one of the few artists who could legitimately claim to be Elvis Presley's successor as the King of Pop, is a fitting tribute.

Spike Lee is himself being honored at Venice where he has had a constant presence since his film Clockers was shown in competition in 1995. His film career has spanned 30 years and covered a range of political and social issues with ingenuity, creativity and courage.  See full press conference interview with Spike Lee & Review of BAD25 on myETVmedia.

snippet.title: BRAZIL: MICHAEL JACKSON IN DONA MARTA SLUM FILMING NEW VIDEO
snippet.description:
(12 Feb 1996) Natural Sound 
Pop star Michael Jackson has travelled to Brazil where he'll record scenes for his new music video in one of the country's most miserable slums.
The video, filmed in Rio de Janeiro's Dona Marta slum, has drawn praise from the city's poor but criticism from civic leaders.
They fear the filming would give Rio a bad image and might hurt its chances of playing host to the 2004 Olympics.
Michael Jackson fans and the international press gathered at Rio de Janeiro's Dona Marta slum, waiting for the pop star to arrive.
Residents had spent Friday and Saturday cleaning and preparing for the moment when their hero would land in a helicopter at a local soccer field.
Getting a taste of what was to come, a Michael imitator entertained the waiting fans with his home-made Jackson performance.
The Dona Marta slum, home to about 13-thousand people, is tucked away in Rio's fashionable south side.
It doesn't appear on official maps, despite its proximity to the mayor's palace.
Rio officials, who are battling high crime and widespread poverty, are eager to promote the city as a tourist paradise.
The video could undermine their efforts and they tried to block the filming.
They feared the publicity would give Rio a bad image and might hurt its chances of playing host to the 2004 Olympics.
But in the end, a judge decided to allow the filming - to the delight of the slum dwellers who want the world to see and recognise their living conditions.
Security had been stepped up for Jackson's visit - producers had hired 50 Dona Marta residents at 70 U-S dollar each to protect director Spike Lee and the singer.
Another 80 officers were put in action by the local police.
When the pop star finally arrived, elated fans tried to get a glimpse of their idol, some making desperate efforts to shake hands with the singer.
Walking through a slum alley, Jackson was accompanied by two children who'd been travelling with him.
Then it was time for the show - with Lee directing the cameramen to get the best shots and Jackson giving his usual performance of dance and movements.
The slum-dwellers are overjoyed with Jackson's new video, one fan believes the place will never be the same again.
Jackson is a hero for the people who live in the slum. 
They believe by coming to their home, the singer proves he cares about their suffering, while the city officials never come up to check it out. 
The video, scheduled for a March release, is to include two or three scenes from Dona Marta. 
The video will also include footage from another Brazilian city and the tough New York neighbourhood of the Bronx.
Jackson's song "They Don't Care About Us" deals with violence and police brutality.

snippet.description: Over 200,000 people took over Fort Greene Park in Brooklyn for Spike Lee’s annual BK Loves MJ Block Party!  Celebrating the King of Pop’s birthday on August 29, 2026, this turned out to be one of the largest outdoor tributes in NYC history. Presented alongside Jordan Brand, the energy was unmatched with legendary mixes spun by DJ Spinna, surprise guest appearances, electric dance-offs, and pure celebration of Michael Jackson’s timeless legacy.  From lifelong fans to the new generation, the entire community came together to prove that "Spreading 💜 is the Brooklyn Way." Check out the wild energy, best outfits, and full crowd reactions from this historic event!

snippet.title: Behind the Scenes in Bahia – Michael Jackson & Spike Lee Filming “They Don’t Care About Us”
snippet.description:
Spike Lee delivers a keynote in Brazil including about the making of Michael Jackson's they don't care about us. Filmed in Rio de Janeiro and Salvador Bahia, Brazil.

Spike Lee is a legend in cinema and his talk in Rio de Janeiro was electric. Watch as he discusses the importance of cinema, the creative process in filmmaking, Brazilian film and the Afro Brazilian cinema movement. Politics and the importance of creativity in storytelling are also discussed in this powerful talk.

Spike Lee in Rio de Janeiro - Part 1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TXV8V...

snippet.title: Brooklyn celebrates Michael Jackson I BK Loves MJ presented by Spike Lee
snippet.description:
"BK Loves MJ" is an iconic, annual block party hosted by Oscar-winning filmmaker Spike Lee to celebrate the life, music, and legacy of Michael Jackson.This years celebration took place in Brooklyn;s Fort Greene Park, marking what would have been the King of Pop's 68th birthday.

The 2026 event marked a highly anticipated return to a live, in-person block party at Fort Greene Park following a multi-year hiatus. Brooklyn royalty DJ Spinna served as the master of the decks for the seven-hour marathon event. He spun a massive catalogue of Jackson 5 classics, solo masterpieces, deep cuts, and rare edits.

The free, public event transformed the park into a massive open-air dance floor. It drew generations of fans, complete with MJ impersonators, vintage merchandise, and elaborate tribute outfits.

snippet.title: Spike Lee on where he'll be Oscar night, Michael Jackson documentary
snippet.description: Two-time nominee and honorary Oscar recipient Spike Lee revealed on Instagram that he and his wife won't attend Sunday's ceremony. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced in January it will take historic action to make its membership more inclusive, but Lee thinks the problem goes much deeper. Lee joins “CBS This Morning” to discuss diversity in the entertainment industry and his new documentary, "Michael Jackson's Journey from Motown to Off the Wall."

snippet.title: Spike Lee’s MJ Block Party August 29, 2026 (some highlights)
snippet.description:
I must admit, I had no intentions of sharing these videos as I took them yesterday. They are far from good quality. But after spending 7 hours doing nothing but singing, dancing, and being in community with other humans who loving and celebrating MJ, I simply had to share some clips. For those of you who weren't there, I hope they give you some joy and (perhaps?) incentive to come next year! It's definitely worth a trip! 

If you're new to this channel, Reading Michael Jackson is an audio only podcast dedicated to further understanding and respecting Michael Jackson as a human being, as well as the greatest entertainer of all time.

snippet.title: Was Michael Jackson’s Real Voice Deeper Than We Think?
snippet.description:
👇We Have A Patreon!👇
https://patreon.com/didyoucatchthis

Was Michael Jackson’s Real Voice Deeper Than We Think?

For decades, Michael Jackson was known not only for his groundbreaking music and electrifying performances but also for his soft-spoken, high-pitched speaking voice — a vocal trademark nearly as iconic as the moonwalk. But over the years, many people who knew or worked with Jackson have claimed that the voice fans heard in interviews wasn't his natural one at all.

According to those close to him, including bodyguards and collaborators, Jackson's real voice was actually much deeper — a rich baritone he reportedly used in private. Some say he kept up the high-pitched tone publicly as part of his carefully crafted persona, maintaining an air of childlike innocence and mystery.

Clips have occasionally surfaced of Jackson speaking in a noticeably lower register, fueling speculation and curiosity. One of the most talked-about moments came during an outtake from a rehearsal or behind-the-scenes footage where Jackson briefly drops into a deeper voice — only to return to his familiar soft tone seconds later.

Whether it was part of the show or simply a deeply personal choice, the idea that the King of Pop's real voice was hidden in plain sight only adds to the mystique surrounding him. As with so many aspects of Michael Jackson’s life, the truth may forever remain part of his legend.
